title: Start Journaling
coreMove: Write the noisy thought down, split the event from the story, and use the page to test the claim before emotion gets to drive.

exampleSpecs.audience: Yves, an auto shop service manager catching his own story mid-note
exampleSpecs.stakes: A lunch grievance may become the tone of the next repair-bay conversation.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Yves notices his own error before the fix becomes the center of the scene.

exampleSpecs.audience: Beckett, a lifeguard lead writing before the next safety call
exampleSpecs.stakes: A prideful story could make the next whistle harsher than the facts require.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The memo carries the action and shows private judgment before public action.

exampleSpecs.audience: Cyrille and Delphine, two rehearsal volunteers handling the same late sign-up sheet
exampleSpecs.stakes: One volunteer reacts to a fresh insult; the other sees a repeatable handoff failure.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Two named people approach one situation in opposite ways and the outcomes diverge.

exampleSpecs.audience: Fabrice, a route driver being coached by Wallace after a late load
exampleSpecs.stakes: A dirty shift can become a blame speech or a weighed claim.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A peer reframe changes Fabrice's stuck view in one conversation.

exampleSpecs.audience: Tristan, a pharmacy trainee learning how to log a tense customer exchange
exampleSpecs.stakes: A learner may confuse a customer's frustration with a personal verdict.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The learner's confusion becomes the material in an onboarding moment.

exampleSpecs.audience: Yves, the same service manager seeing a repair-bay problem with one variable changed
exampleSpecs.stakes: A recurring equipment snag can stay personal or become a process fix.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The same person and process appear twice with the written record as the changed variable.
